newsitem.title: USA: Amylin licenses Gila monster compound.
newsitem.headline: Amylin licenses Gila monster compound.

text.p: Amylin Pharmaceuticals Inc said on Monday it had acquired exclusive patent rights to a newly discovered compound found in the venom of the Gila monster lizard.
The compound, licensed from its discoverer Dr. John Eng of The Bronx, New York, shows potential as a drug for treating diabetes, Amylin said.

Known as "exendin," the compound has been shown to have effects known to be important for improving glucose control, the company said. These include stimulation of secretion of insulin, a hormone that lowers blood glucose.
It has also been shown to slow the entry of ingested sugars into the bloodstream.
Presumably as a result of these actions, exendin has exhibited glucose-lowering effects in an animal model of diabetes, the company said.
Exendin could be important in developing a new class of medicines that correct certain hormonal and metabolic disorders characteristic of diabetes, Amylin said.
